historyTimeline.h2: Honda Civic 2.2 i-DTEC - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: Launched as the highly efficient, long-distance diesel option in the Civic range, the 2.2 i-DTEC variant spanned the 8th and 9th generations, offering robust torque and excellent fuel economy before being phased out in favour of the smaller 1.6 i-DTEC unit.

milestones.description: N22A2, 2.2L Diesel, 140PS (103kW) - Introduced in the 8th generation Civic (FN/FK), providing a powerful and economical diesel option for EX and EX-S trims.
N22B2, 2.2L Diesel, 150PS (110kW) - 9th generation launch brought an updated i-DTEC engine with revised emissions technology, improved refinement, and a slight power increase for EX and Type S trims.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Honda Civic 2.2 i-DTEC is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Honda Civic 2.2 i-DTEC Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Honda Civic 2.2 i-DTEC is generally a robust and reliable diesel unit, but high-mileage examples are prone to specific emissions-related wear points. The N22A2 and N22B2 codes dominate replacement demand for this variant due to DPF and EGR-related failures. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: DPF Clogging & EGR Failure - Why the Honda Civic 2.2 i-DTEC (N22A2/N22B2) Restricts Airflow
problems.rootCause: Short urban journeys prevent the DPF from completing active regeneration cycles, while exhaust gases recirculated by the EGR valve deposit heavy carbon soot, restricting airflow and triggering limp mode.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Chemical DPF clean and EGR maintenance.
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable for early-stage clogging, but does not fix underlying mechanical wear.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call when carbon damage has caused secondary issues like turbo starvation or severe compression loss.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Honda Civic 2.2 i-DTEC (8th/9th gen, 2006-2017) currently holds a UK market value of approximately £2,000 to £7,000 [THIRD-PARTY]. - Vehicle worth under ~£5,000: repair or used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. - Vehicle worth ~£5,000-£8,000: evaluate both; reconditioned is viable if keeping the car 2+ years. - Vehicle worth ~£8,000-£15,000: reconditioned/rebuilt usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. - Vehicle worth £15,000+: replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value. Note for Honda Civic 2.2 i-DTEC: Given the typical value band (£2,000-£7,000), a full rebuilt engine (£2,500+) frequently approaches or exceeds the vehicle's total market value for older 8th-generation models. If the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate scrap value before committing.
problems.recommendation: For most Honda Civic 2.2 i-DTEC owners, a targeted component repair (DPF clean, EGR service, or injector replacement) offers the best financial return if the engine block is fundamentally sound. However, if the engine has suffered catastrophic turbo debris ingestion or severe internal wear, sourcing a low-mileage used engine is often the most economically viable path, provided it comes with a verifiable warranty.

items.question: What are the common signs of Honda Civic 2.2 i-DTEC engine failure?
items.answer: Owners of the Honda Civic 2.2 i-DTEC should watch for persistent limp mode, excessive black smoke from the exhaust, and a noticeable loss of power under acceleration.
keyPoints: A rough idle or misfire often indicates failing injectors or severe DPF clogging.
If the engine management light is flashing alongside these symptoms, stop driving immediately.
Continuing to drive can cause catastrophic internal damage to the turbocharger or engine block.

items.question: Is it worth replacing the engine in an older Honda Civic 2.2 i-DTEC?
items.answer: Given that 8th and 9th generation Honda Civic 2.2 i-DTEC models typically hold a market value between £2,000 and £7,000, a full rebuilt engine can cost more than the car is worth.
keyPoints: For most owners of older models, sourcing a verified low-mileage used engine is the most financially sensible option.
Investing in targeted component repairs (like a DPF clean or injector replacement) is also viable if the engine block is healthy.
A rebuilt unit is only recommended if you plan to keep the vehicle long-term and it holds exceptional condition.

items.question: What is the difference between the N22A2 and N22B2 engine codes in the Honda Civic 2.2 i-DTEC?
items.answer: The N22A2 code was used in the 8th generation Civic (2006-2012) and produces 140PS.
keyPoints: The N22B2 code was introduced in the 9th generation (2012-2017) with an increased output of 150PS and revised emissions technology.
Although they share the same 2.2L architecture, their ECU mapping and minor component specs differ.
Always verify your exact engine code via your V5C logbook or registration before ordering a replacement.
